chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has a partner, and it becomes apparent to him that his partner has cheated him in something. Is it permissible for him to take from him the equivalent of what was taken, without making that clear? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is good for them if they partnered in the trust of Allah, and I like for him, if he sees something of that from him, to conceal it from him, and I do not like for him to take anything from him without his knowledge.'

key_terms.يَسْتُرَ عَلَيْهِ: to conceal it from him (cover his fault)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred ethical conduct when a business partner suspects dishonesty from their partner?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the ethical standard of commercial partnership by prioritizing *sitr* (concealment of faults) over strict financial retribution. He advises that since partners share in the 'trust of Allah,' it is preferable to overlook minor dishonesty rather than deducting an equivalent amount secretly, thereby preserving the spiritual bond of the partnership. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab al-mu'amalat* (etiquette of dealings) and maintaining harmony within the community.
